text:
mira: Hey team — found a partner debug dump in GCS that contains a wrapped keystore blob and a couple of truncated connection strings. not sure if unwrapped material leaked. pinging sec.
sam: Ack. Can you paste the GCS path (no creds) and the heap of filenames we saw? we should immediately silo access and stop any automated restores.
mira: gs://partner-logs/2026-03-20/debug-archive.tar.gz -> inside: keystore.wrapped (160kb), app-prod.log (contains partial connstr: postgres://redacted@...).
security-bot: Incident classifier: potential credential exposure — severity: medium -> escalate if any service account keys are present.
jordan: Steps I'm thinking: 1) revoke any SA tokens that might've written that bucket (short-term deny). 2) rotate the KMS wrapping key used to produce keystore.wrapped. 3) snapshot current Vault transit key policy and rewrap only after verifying backups.
kai: Also block partner read access on that bucket, preserve object at time-of-discovery (dont delete). create a locked copy for forensics.
mira: Done: partner bucket ACL set to private at 12:03 UTC. Locked copy created at gs://redwood-incidents/7162348000-locked-copy.tar.gz
sam: For rotation: propose wrap-key rekey policy — create new key version, rewrap ciphertext with new key, then re-issue secrets to services. We must avoid mass re-issue until we confirm which secrets are impacted.
jordan: Agreed. Can we do a safe rehydration run for one non-critical service first? Example commands below (dry-run):
```
# create new key version
gcloud kms keys versions create --key=keystore-wrap --location=global --keyring=redwood-kr

# rewrap artifact (example using openssl + gcloud kms)
cat keystore.wrapped | gcloud kms decrypt --location=global --keyring=redwood-kr --key=keystore-wrap --ciphertext-file=- > /tmp/keystore.raw
# re-encrypt with new key version
gcloud kms encrypt --location=global --keyring=redwood-kr --key=keystore-wrap --plaintext-file=/tmp/keystore.raw --ciphertext-file=keystore.rewrapped
```
Note: above path placeholders, do in isolated host with temp creds.
kai: For Vault+KMS workflow: we should avoid decrypting the keystore on any host that has network access to production. Instead use an offline forensics VM that we control, with ephemeral auth to KMS, and record nonce for audit. Then re-issue via Vault API patch to targeted mounts.
mira: For the audit trail — I've opened a ticket in Jira (#SEC-8342) and linked the locked copy. We need a short timeline of actions for the customer team and for legal.
sam: Action items (who/when):
- mira: preserve artifacts, share locked copy with forensics (done) — due: now
- jordan: spin an offline rewrap VM + run dry rewrap for dev service (test) — due: +2h
- kai: block partner access + request partner to rotate their ingest credentials and upload proof — due: +1h
- security-bot: run KMS key usage audit for last 30 days and post findings here.
jordan: One more: plan to rotate Vault transit key config only after verifying that rewrapped artifact decrypts cleanly and services can read from a staging mount. no force-rotate on prod mounts yet.
mira: FYI backup plan: if rewrap fails, we will fallback to sticking with current key and instead mark impacted secrets as rotated at the service layer (i.e., reissue credentials from upstream providers). but let's try rewrap first.
kai: I'll ping partner slack contact and request rotation proof, and ask them to provide the object creation logs for the bucket (to check if exfil occurred). @mira can you paste the object metadata here?
mira: object metadata snippet: size=163840, created=2026-03-20T09:12:04Z, acl=PUBLIC_READ previously (rotated to private at discovery), crc32c=5f3a1b2c.
security-bot: KMS audit job triggered by request. ETA ~18m. Will post log hits and principal list.
sam: When KMS audit hits come back, if we see the wrapping key used by unexpected principals, escalate to legal + infra. Otherwise continue with controlled rewrap.
jordan: If we need to force rekey, follow churn policy: create new key, create new key version, set primary -> rewrap latent ciphertexts on controlled VM, then rotate Vault transit alias to new key. communicate maintenance window to infra.
mira: Good. I'll keep this thread updated with forensics output. please add any additional blockers. :thumbsup:
